5 Most Common Bitcoin Misconceptions

Posted on March 16, 2016 by Natasha Gan

Most people have heard of Bitcoin but chances are, only a small portion of them actually know much about the cryptocurrency. To help understand what Bitcoin is and what it’s not, we’ve rounded up the five most common bitcoin misconceptions.

So what is Bitcoin? Bitcoin is a payment system created in 2008 by an anonymous coder (or a group) called Satoshi Nakamoto. It runs on a peer-to-peer (decentralized) network called the blockchain. Unlike our traditional fiat currencies, Bitcoin is not issued or controlled by a central authority like banks or governments.

5 Most Common Bitcoin Misconceptions

1. Bitcoins have no value

As a currency, Bitcoin is valuable because it’s a useful means of exchange. It has all the characteristics of money: durability, scarcity, divisibility, portability and acceptability. Its value also lies in its ability to solve the problems we face with existing currencies and banking system. For example, bitcoins can be transferred across international borders within minutes. Transaction fees are extremely low and there are no taxes involved. The demand and supply of bitcoins is what determines its price. It fluctuates a lot but at the time of writing, 1 BTC is worth around CAD $555, one indicator that there’s ample demand for the cryptocurrency.

2. Bitcoins are unregulated and are therefore unsafe

Though Bitcoins aren’t issued by a central authority, it’s not exactly accurate to say it’s unregulated. We have regulations and rules for other similar things that would apply to bitcoin. In general, Bitcoin is a trustless system as it is governed by pure mathematics and algorithms. All transactions are recorded in a public ledger called the blockchain. A network of nodes maintain the integrity of the blockchain by validating transactions and announcing each change to other nodes, and a change only occurs when there is consensus.

3. Bitcoin has been hacked

Another common bitcoin misconception is that it’s hackable. The bitcoin protocol has never lost customers’ funds; it’s the third parties that have held on to other people’s bitcoins that have been hacked. The great thing about bitcoin is that you can be your own bank without having to rely on other people.

4. It’s a currency used exclusively for illegal purchases

Bitcoin has had its fair share of bad publicity. It has been associated with criminal activities in the past but its uses are more diverse than some may think. You can book flights and hotels using BTCtrip.com, you can save money on Amazon using Purse.io and purchase anything from bed sheets to watches on Overstock.com.

5. Bitcoins are difficult to use

Contrary to popular belief, bitcoin isn’t intimidating to deal with. To buy bitcoins, you simply download a bitcoin wallet app on your phone and find the nearest Bitcoin ATM. We have a two-way machine at our office that lets you buy and sell bitcoins with cash. The process is easy and takes less than five minutes (with extra confirmation time needed). In fact, it’s comparable to using a regular ATM. First timers can check our FAQ page here.

With these common bitcoin misconceptions cleared up, you should be moving on from asking “what is Bitcoin?” to asking “why not bitcoin?”
